newsitem.title: USA: Virginia executes killer on Human Rights Day.
newsitem.headline: Virginia executes killer on Human Rights Day.

text.p: Virginia late Tuesday executed Larry Allen Stout, who killed a mother of two by stabbing her in the neck during a robbery.
Stout was pronounced dead at 9:12 p.m., an official said.
Stout, 33, admitted killing Jacqueline Kooshian, owner and operator of Trimble's Cleaners in Staunton Feb. 17, 1987.
Stout spent his last day visiting with lawyers and ministers. He ordered sausage pizza, french fries and cherry pie for his last meal.
The Supreme Court turned down his last appeal Tuesday afternoon and Virginia Gov. George Allen announced later in the day that he would not intercede.
"One of the most fundamental human rights is the right to live one's life free from deadly criminal violence inflicted by others," Allen said in a statement.

The timing of the execution, on International Human Rights Day, sparked a protest at the state Capitol in Richmond Tuesday afternoon. Another was planned Tuesday night outside the Greensville Correctional Centre, where the execution took place.
Stout was sixth person executed in Virginia this year.
